decisions_this_run: D-058a: the diagnostic describes the claim SHAPE and never a claim value. acr is an IdP-chosen class name and amr can name methods personal to the account; the shape answers the operator's question without putting a claim value in the log.
D-058b: the line fires only when the derivation lands below STEP_UP_FLOOR. A satisfying login logs nothing, so the signal does not drown on every normal MFA login.

D-058c: the acr marker scan is shared by enforcement and the diagnostic so the two cannot disagree about which segment is the marker. It returns EVERY marker and the veto applies per-marker: a first version returned only the first marker, which would have silently changed enforcement for mfa-optional:multi-factor.

head_drift_policy: `commit` names the last head whose *product* code was verified by CI, not necessarily the branch tip. NEXUS checkpoint updates are themselves docs-only commits, so the tip advances one commit past `commit` every time this file is written - chasing it is an unbounded loop (run 64 hit this: 7456a89 -> 974d03f -> c49befe, each fix creating a new tip). On reconciliation, compare the product tree, not the SHA: `git diff <commit>..HEAD -- src/ tests/` being empty means `commit` is still an accurate description of what CI verified.
